references.text: The same ritual of dipping the finger in blood and sprinkling it seven times before the Lord is described earlier in the chapter for the priest's sin offering.
Moses sprinkles the blood seven times on the altar at the consecration of the tabernacle, the same ritual action with sevenfold sprinkling.
In the cleansing of leprosy, the priest shall sprinkle seven times, following the same ritual pattern of sevenfold sprinkling.
The priest dips his finger in oil and sprinkles it seven times before the face of the Lord, a parallel action involving the finger and sevenfold sprinkling.
On the Day of Atonement, the high priest sprinkles blood seven times with his finger before the mercy seat, the same ritual action.
The blood from the goat is sprinkled seven times before the mercy seat, parallel to the sprinkling before the veil.
The priest sprinkles blood from the red heifer seven times toward the tent of meeting, following the same ritual pattern.
The veil (parokhet) mentioned here is the same veil that was made according to God's instructions to Moses.
Hebrews refers to the blood sprinkling in the old covenant and how Christ's blood is superior for cleansing the conscience.
Refers to the sprinkling of blood on the tabernacle and all its service vessels, and that without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
